exactEuRule.result: Outside acceleration areas, when the relevant EIA is required, the authority must issue an opinion defining scope/detail; the scope cannot subsequently be extended. The provision specifies no separate numerical deadline for giving that opinion.
exactEuRule.retrieval: Fresh official indexed authentic text read; direct browser/PDF endpoints returned anti-bot content or an empty download. The full relevant paragraph was available in the official search result.

July2026 permits earlier requests during consultation. But4 preserves all other functions and prevents reliance on the opinion in planning/legal proceedings; the new specific non-extension rule3B remains deferred. This is positive contrary statutory text, beyond mere omission of new words.

Existing request-led duties already require opinions before the application/report, and reports must be based on them. Paragraphs b expressly preserve further-information powers. The mandatory applicant-request and express non-extension rules ab are deferred. Those pre-existing duties establish a real scoping route, but no independently identified binding limit equivalent to the specific new guarantee.

Alternative enacted framework remains request-led; report consistency/reasonably required information and further-information powers coexist. Its exact current commencement was not independently exhaustively established in this focused pass; even assuming applicable, its text alone supplies no demonstrated fixed-scope equivalence.

guidanceAndLimits.assessment: Current-facing guide confirms November mandatory start and says no numerical scoping deadline exists. It describes the non-extension rule but also says material changes beyond scoped design parameters with different/additional likely significant effects can require fresh scoping. Its express guidance-only status and future-start explanation do not establish the deferred rule is already a binding domestic guarantee. concreteResidual: A developer could use the current statutory route without requesting a scoping opinion; the revised EU framework requires an opinion when the relevant EIA is required.

For a requested opinion on an unchanged, adequately described project, the older binding framework contains non-reliance/further-information reservations rather than an identified prohibition on later expansion. The express new limit is still deferred.

Existing requested scoping supplies much of the result, and EU-derived enforceability/conforming interpretation may protect individuals. No practical widening, missed deadline, project delay or denial of an enforceable EU right has been established.

proposedTargetedEdits.euChange: For relevant renewable projects outside acceleration areas requiring EIA, Article16b(2) requires a scoping opinion and limits subsequent enlargement of its scope.
proposedTargetedEdits.nationalGapAddition: Existing sections37D and173 already require an opinion when requested and require the report to be based on it. Section37D(4) nevertheless preserves other powers and prevents reliance on the opinion; section173 preserves further-information powers. The specific mandatory coverage and non-extension protections are the deferred changes.
proposedTargetedEdits.caveatAddition: This does not mean no binding scoping procedure exists. Further information within the agreed scope remains distinct from enlarging it; materially changed projects producing new or different likely significant effects may require fresh scoping. No general immunity from further environmental information is claimed.
